<p>“Hmph.”</p><p>The sparring was over.</p><p>It had been a long time since he’d had a pure sparring match—one meant to compare strength rather than kill the opponent.</p><p>In general, the American Hunter Association’s members had good manners, so no real incidents occurred.</p><p>He had sparred with seven A-rank Hunters from the U.S., one after another, and hadn’t landed a single damaging blow on any of them.</p><p>Whenever they attacked, he would dodge or block, and if he found an opening, he’d lightly tap that spot with his palm.</p><p>It was an implicit way of saying, *You would’ve died just now.* And they seemed to understand, because each time that happened, they’d acknowledge their loss and step back.</p><p>The only slightly annoying part was that after each sparring session, they’d bow in the Japanese style before leaving.</p><p>He knew they didn’t mean any harm, so he couldn’t bring himself to get angry.</p><p>In fact, he could relate.</p><p>It was almost comforting to see that Hunters on both sides were just as broke.</p><p>The American Hunters were now saying something to the interpreter.</p><p>“Vice President.”</p><p>“Yes?”</p><p>“The American Hunters are having a party tonight, and they’d really like to invite you.”</p><p>“Would it be alright for me to go?”</p><p>“Yes, today’s schedule is already finished, so it’s fine. They seem… quite excited after sparring with you.”</p><p>“Hmm… Give me a moment.”</p><p>He called Yoon Na-hyeon first, but she said she had a lot to do and would probably be working at the U.S. Hunter Association headquarters until dawn.</p><p>Next, he called Seong Yu-na, who said she wouldn’t be able to return to the hotel tonight.</p><p>When he asked why, she explained that Echo and Nerus were completely hooked on the casino and would likely be up all night there.</p><p>“Casino…?”</p><p>He asked if they couldn’t just use magic to cheat and win, but Echo and Nerus had apparently scoffed at the idea, saying that if they used magic, it wouldn’t be a fair match. They insisted that the fun of gambling came from psychological warfare and skill, so they’d sat down at the table.</p><p>And now, three hours later, they’d lost all the money they’d exchanged for chips, recharged their chips, and were back at the table.</p><p>He’d been worried that Yu-na and Yoon Ji-hyeon might be struggling, but they both said the casino was fun.</p><p>Nerus had used telepathy to contact Han Ji-hyeok, who had booked a suite at the casino hotel where Yu-na was playing, so they didn’t have to worry about lodging.</p><p>The thought of the emperor who had once looked down on humans as mere insects—now getting fleeced by local gamblers—was almost too funny.</p><p>Apparently, Nerus had more talent for cards than Echo.</p><p>Echo had already lost all his chips, recharged, and was back at the table, but Nerus was holding his own.</p><p>At this rate, even if I go back to the hotel today, there’s no one waiting for me. I’ll just be alone.</p><p>“Please tell them I’m grateful for the invitation and that I’ll come.”</p><p>“Yes, Vice President.”</p><p>***</p><p>“This is different.”</p><p>The party was being held in a building rented for the occasion, where Hunters had gathered.</p><p>Attending were Hunters and Association members from the American branch.</p><p>Originally, an American S-rank Hunter was supposed to join the party, but I heard they had to cancel due to a sudden urgent matter.</p><p>Since I can’t speak English, an interpreter had offered to stay, but I felt bad for overworking them, so I sent them home.</p><p>For the male staff who came as my driver and aide, I booked them a room at a nearby hotel and told them to rest up, not to drink, and to call me when the party was over. I even gave them my card and told them to order whatever they wanted to eat.</p><p>I’d been worried about the language barrier, but the party turned out to be more fun than I expected.</p><p>The drinks for Hunters, called Drops, were strictly separated from the alcohol for regular people.</p><p>They had me step up onto a podium and asked me to say a few words.</p><p>I just shouted in Korean, “Let’s have a wild time!” and somehow they seemed to understand, because that’s when the party turned into absolute chaos.</p><p>Surprisingly, after about an hour at the party, my ears started to pick up the language little by little.</p><p>At first, I couldn’t understand a single word, but now I could roughly grasp what they were trying to say.</p><p>If I strung together the few words I knew to respond, they somehow interpreted it correctly.</p><p>I’d once heard that if you drop someone who wants to learn English into an area of America with no Koreatown, they’ll become fluent within a year just to survive. Turns out that was true.</p><p>The first three hours were filled with deafening music that shook the building, with everyone drinking, dancing, and chatting. But as time passed, the atmosphere shifted—people started gathering in small groups, sitting down for more serious conversations.</p><p>It was fun.</p><p>But true to my introverted nature, I was starting to feel drained. I sat in a quiet corner, sipping Drops by myself.</p><p>I’d drunk way more than I had that time with Se-rin when we caused a scene, but I only felt a little buzzed, not drunk.</p><p>That’s when an American Hunter sat down next to me.</p><p>I poured her a glass of Drops, and after she drank it, she smiled and said,</p><p>“How do you like America?”</p><p>“It’s great. I was worried the food wouldn’t suit me, but it’s actually—wait, huh? What?”</p><p>Without thinking, I replied in Korean when I heard the language, but the person in front of me was a blonde, blue-eyed, stereotypical white American woman.</p><p>The woman answered with a smile.</p><p>“I was a diplomat stationed at the Korean Association until last year.”</p><p>“Your Korean is incredibly fluent.”</p><p>“Yes, I studied hard.”</p><p>“If you don’t mind me asking… your name?”</p><p>“Lauren Hayes. Just call me Hayes.”</p><p>“Got it, Hayes. Nice to meet you.”</p><p>Unbelievable.</p><p>Her pronunciation was a little stiff, but her Korean was so fluent that she could pass for a native speaker.</p><p>Hayes and I shared drinks and talked for a long time.</p><p>She said she was an A-rank Hunter from the U.S. and currently worked at the White House.</p><p>She looked to be around thirty, but she was actually thirty-nine. I’d heard white people aged quickly, but Hayes was surprisingly youthful.</p><p>We drank for two hours as she told me stories about her time in Korea.</p><p>When it was time to wrap up, Hayes asked for my number.</p><p>I hesitated for a moment, but since I’d be returning to Korea soon and there was no real reason not to, I gave it to her. It wasn’t like giving my personal number to a White House Hunter would cause any trouble.</p><p>After chatting for another 30 minutes, Hayes said she had to leave since her hotel was nearby.</p><p>As soon as she was gone, a drunk Black man plopped down next to me and started venting about his life.</p><p>I couldn’t catch everything, but from the bits about his wife and daughter, it sounded like he was complaining about the weight of being the head of the household.</p><p>He kept calling me “Walker,” so he must’ve thought I was his friend.</p><p>I nodded along and played along until his friends noticed him, apologized for his drunkenness, and helped him away.</p><p>It was a pretty fun time.</p><p>Just as I was about to call my knights to head out, my phone rang. It was Hayes.</p><p>-Hayes?</p><p>-Sorry. Did I startle you by calling so soon?</p><p>-No, not at all. Was there a reason you called…?</p><p>-Actually, I left my bag at the table where we were drinking. Could you bring it to my hotel room?</p><p>-Your hotel?</p><p>-Yes, it’s right next to the venue. I’ll text you the room number.</p><p>-Got it…</p><p>“Haa…”</p><p>One hundred percent.</p><p>Even if I were a complete idiot, I’d know what’s going on here.</p><p>This is a sure thing.</p><p>Common sense says if she really forgot her bag, she’d ask her fellow Hunters first—not some guy she just met today.</p><p>Maybe… just maybe there was a 0.1% chance that he was just asking me as a favor since I happened to be at the same table.</p><p>As I found Hayes’s bag and stood up to leave, the Black guy who had been drunk and complaining about his life earlier suddenly spotted the bag, jumped in surprise, and started saying something to me as he approached.</p><p>It sounded like he was saying, “You shouldn’t go there.”</p><p>He kept mixing in the word “bro,” but I had no idea what it meant.</p><p>I used my limited English and body language to explain that Hayes had asked me to bring his bag, but the guy broke out in a cold sweat, desperately trying to make me understand by stringing together simple words like “Phishing!” “Phishing!” “Understand?”</p><p>I just nodded vaguely and left.</p><p>Before exiting the party, I glanced back and saw his friends patting his shoulders, giving off the vibe of, “You did all you could. Don’t feel guilty.”</p><p>***</p><p>“Mr. Hayes, I’ve brought your bag.”</p><p>“Thank you. The door’s open, so come in?”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>When I opened the door and stepped inside, sure enough, Hayes was standing in front of the bed, completely naked.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291604" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Uh… here’s your bag.”</p><p>As I turned my head away, set the bag down, and tried to leave, Hayes grabbed my hand and said,</p><p>“You figured it out the moment you got the call, didn’t you?”</p><p>“What? I don’t know what you—”</p><p>“Let’s be honest with each other. Should I go first? I have a preference for sleeping with young men.”</p><p>“I don’t understand what you’re—”</p><p>Hayes licked his lips, then gave me a seductive look as he said,</p><p>“Let me put it in Korean so you’ll understand. I like fucking guys who are at least ten years younger than me.”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>“Back in Korea, I used to go to Itaewon every week without a worry and fuck fresh twentysomethings. But seeing you, Vice President, makes me want to fuck an Asian again after so long.”</p><p>Only now did I understand what the Black guy had been shouting at me.</p><p>He had been saying, “Don’t go there! You’re being played! I’m telling you, don’t go!”</p><p>“Every man I’ve slept with has passed out. I wonder how you’ll do, Vice President.”</p><p>Clink.</p><p>Hayes muttered as he undid my belt.</p>
